name: evaluate_fca_handbook_applicability
description: Evaluate which FCA Handbook entries apply to an entity, via the Metis FCA Handbook AI Harness. One-shot: no session, no conversation state. Supports quick mode (60-120 seconds, default) and full mode (longer, more detailed). Returns a compliance report with verbatim citations, gaps, and refinement suggestions. Uses Claude internally; usage is billed to the account owning the API key (no mark-up on tokens).

setup.instructions: An admin generates an API key from the account dashboard (paid/Stripe accounts only). Set it as the METIS_API_KEY environment variable and use it as a Bearer token.

authentication.bearer_token: API key from the account dashboard (METIS_API_KEY env var), format sk_live_...

endpoint.streaming: Always streams (Server-Sent Events). There is no non-streaming mode.
endpoint.charging: A flat £7.95 is charged immediately on completion, regardless of outcome quality. No mark-up on tokens.

design_principles.single_input_field: There is exactly one input field: user_input (max 5000 characters). No entity_description/question/context split. Put everything in one piece of text.
design_principles.literal_then_semantic: The Harness's Node 2 semantically parses your one user_input blob into structured fields (entity type, the question, etc.) for its own internal pipeline. Be explicit about what you're asking — e.g. end with a clear question — since extraction quality depends on it.
design_principles.stateless: Each request is independent. The calling LLM manages any multi-turn conversation; the Harness has no memory of previous calls.
design_principles.one_shot: One complete analysis per request. To refine, reformulate user_input using refinement_suggestions and call again.
design_principles.streaming_only: The response is always an SSE stream. You will receive 7-8 'message' events (one per reasoning node plus final 'Analysis complete'), interspersed with processing time, then the final 'analysis' or 'error' event. Total time: 60-120 seconds (quick mode) or longer (full mode). This is not a token-by-token reasoning stream.

user_input.description: Everything together, as one piece of text: firm type, regulatory status, products/services, key activities, target market, data handled, and the specific compliance question to answer. Be explicit about the question — e.g. end with 'Question: ...' — since a Haiku call semantically extracts it from this text, and vague phrasing degrades that extraction.

analysis_mode.description: 'quick' is a fast pass identifying the most critical binding obligations. 'full' performs detailed conditional reasoning — each entry's applicability, mandatory vs. conditional obligations, tensions between provisions, second-order gaps — and returns more refinement suggestions (2-4 vs. quick's 1). Full takes longer than quick's 60-120 seconds; use a ~300 second client timeout.

input_schema.notes: There is no separate entity_description, question, or context field. Sending extra fields has no effect — they're silently ignored.

output_schema.format: SSE stream: one 'message' event, then either 'error' or 'analysis'. Only these three event types occur on this endpoint (the web UI's separate /api/chat endpoint has a richer set that does NOT apply here).

message_types.message: Progress notification: one per node (7-8 total in a typical run, including final 'Analysis complete'). Each contains a human-readable description of what's happening.
message_types.error: Terminal. content is a plain string: budget-exceeded message, an out-of-scope rejection from the triage gate, or str(exception) for any other failure. No structured error code.
message_types.analysis: Terminal, success case. content is the object described below.

summary.description: 2-3 sentence synthesis of what applies and why.

entry_analysis.description: One entry per retrieved FCA Handbook entry: {entry_id, entry_text, applies, conditional, reasoning}.

obligations.description: {high_confidence: [], conditional_obligations: [], low_confidence_or_tangential: []} — each an array of {obligation, type}.

gaps.description: Array of {gap, why_it_matters} — what the analysis couldn't resolve.

refinement_suggestions.description: Array of {suggestion, priority}. Use these to decide what to ask next if refining.

citations.description: Array of {entry_id, cited_text, binding_level} — binding_level is R (Rule), G (Guidance), or E (Evidential).

tokens.description: {input, output, total} — token counts for this run, for cost/complexity transparency. Not the billed amount (that's a flat £7.95 regardless of token count).

http_level.401: Missing/malformed Authorization header, or the API key is invalid/revoked.
http_level.404: The key's account no longer exists.
http_level.422: user_input missing from the request body.
http_level.500: Deployment misconfiguration, not a caller issue.

error_handling.in_stream: Everything else (budget exceeded, out-of-scope question, Harness failure) arrives as an SSE 'error' event over HTTP 200, not as an HTTP error status. There is no 429 rate limiting implemented.
error_handling.recovery: On 'error', read content as plain text and decide whether it's actionable (e.g. rephrase an out-of-scope question) or terminal (e.g. budget exceeded — nothing to retry).

initial_shot.step_1_collect_input: Collect everything into one piece of text: firm/product/service details plus the specific compliance question.
initial_shot.step_2_call_api: POST to /v1/analyze with the Bearer token and {"user_input": "..."}.
initial_shot.step_3_read_stream: Parse SSE lines. Expect one 'message' event, then wait (60-120s) for 'analysis' or 'error'.
initial_shot.step_4_extract_results: On 'analysis', read summary, entry_analysis, obligations, gaps, refinement_suggestions, citations, tokens.

refinement_loop.step_5_read_suggestions: refinement_suggestions tells you what's worth asking next.
refinement_loop.step_6_offer_to_user: Offer the suggestion(s) to the user; let them decide whether to refine.
refinement_loop.step_7_reformulate_and_repeat: If refining, weave the new detail into a single new user_input string and call again — a new, independent request. No history is kept.

calling_pattern.key_points: The calling LLM owns the conversation. The Harness is one-shot and stateless. analysis_mode defaults to 'quick'; ask the user if 'full' seems warranted (they're weighing a significant decision, or quick's summary left real gaps) rather than defaulting to it — it takes longer. There is no rate limiting to plan around today.

examples.python_request:
import json
import requests
import os

api_key = os.getenv('METIS_API_KEY')
response = requests.post(
    'https://fcahandbookharnessimplementation.onrender.com/v1/analyze',
    headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {api_key}'},
    json={
        'user_input': 'Robo-advisor platform... Question: What FCA authorisation do we need?'
    },
    stream=True,
    timeout=180,
)

result = None
for line in response.iter_lines():
    if not line or not line.startswith(b'data:'):
        continue
    event = json.loads(line[len(b'data:'):].decode('utf-8'))
    if event['type'] == 'analysis':
        result = event['content']
    elif event['type'] == 'error':
        raise RuntimeError(event['content'])

print(result['summary'])
print('Refinement suggestions:', result['refinement_suggestions'])
print('Tokens used:', result['tokens']['total'])

key_insights: user_input is required; analysis_mode ('quick' or 'full', default 'quick') is optional. No entity_description/question/context split.
This is NOT a token-by-token reasoning stream. It's one 'message' event, a long wait, then the final 'analysis' or 'error' event.
Be explicit about the question inside user_input — a Haiku call semantically extracts it, and vague phrasing produces worse retrieval.
refinement_suggestions tell you what to ask next; you decide whether to refine or conclude.
tokens is for cost/complexity transparency only — billing is a flat £7.95 per call regardless of token count.
Stateless, one-shot: no session ID, no history. Each call is independent.

Verbatim citations from the FCA Handbook, not generative invention — but entry_analysis/citations can legitimately come back empty if retrieval didn't find a strong match; that's not necessarily an error.
